title: COAXIAL: A CXL-Centric Memory System for Scalable Servers
problem: DDR's large pin requirements limit processor memory bandwidth, and multiple concurrent memory requests experience significant queuing delays that degrade performance in manycore servers.
motivation: Growing core counts and datasets demand higher memory bandwidth and capacity to sustain server performance.
method: CoaXial replaces all processor DDR interfaces with CXL interface, which offers 4x higher bandwidth per pin. The system carefully integrates CXL to offset its latency overhead with superior bandwidth characteristics, demonstrating that bandwidth gains overcome the latency cost for many workloads.
key_novelty: Using CXL as the primary memory interface for servers instead of DDR, leveraging its superior pin efficiency to provide 4x higher bandwidth-per-pin despite higher latency.
contributions: Demonstrates viability of CXL as primary memory interface for manycore servers
Shows CXL's bandwidth advantages offset its latency overhead for throughput-oriented workloads
Achieves 1.39x average and up to 3x performance improvement over DDR-based systems
limitations: The paper acknowledges CXL's considerable latency overhead but does not discuss other architectural or deployment limitations.
primary_theme: CXL-based memory architecture for high-bandwidth servers
